title: LIGHT AND SHADOW EXPRESSION: Contrast, Luminosity, Porosity
central_proposition: This thesis advocates for the integration and expression of light and shadow as a qualitative architectural design medium to create perceptually fluid, stimulating, and enriching environments that support user experience and well-being, challenging the prevailing quantitative design evaluation in contemporary architecture.

concept_definitions.name: Light
concept_definitions.definition: Provides visual stimulation enabling perception and experience of the world, manifesting through interaction with material.

concept_definitions.name: Darkness/Shadow
concept_definitions.definition: Reduces visual sharpness, heightens other senses, makes depth and distance, and invites unconscious peripheral vision and tactile fantasy; a result of light being unable to transmit through material.

concept_definitions.name: Qualitative Lighting Design
concept_definitions.definition: Examines light's experiential characteristics and its influence on the human body, perception, architectural environment, and experience.

concept_definitions.name: Quantifiable Metrics
concept_definitions.definition: A scientific approach to light integration, examining it through energy and required illumination for task performance.

concept_definitions.name: Focal Glow
concept_definitions.definition: The focal spatial illumination within a space, a highly illuminated object that commands attention.

concept_definitions.name: Ambient Luminescence
concept_definitions.definition: The overall spatial illumination created through indirect or direct illumination.

concept_definitions.name: Play of Brilliance
concept_definitions.definition: A lighting spectacle where the expression of light evokes a sense of imagination and wonder.

argument_structure: The argument begins by establishing the fundamental significance of light and shadow for human perception and experience, critiquing contemporary architecture's over-reliance on homogeneous, quantifiable lighting. It then traces historical and modern approaches to light integration, emphasizing the qualitative aspects of contrast, luminosity, and porosity. The thesis proposes five design strategies (solar orientation, artificial illumination, architectural form, material properties, spatial ambiance) to creatively express light and shadow, culminating in a design project that illustrates these concepts in an office hub.
mechanism_or_causal_logic: The core mechanism is that dynamic and varied light and shadow conditions provide continuous sensorial and perceptual stimulation, engaging the human eye, mind, and body. This variability, influenced by natural (solar patterns, circadian rhythms) and artificial light, as well as architectural form and material properties, prevents habituation and enriches the architectural experience. In contrast, homogeneous lighting deprives users of this stimulation, leading to reduced well-being and a diminished sense of place. Specific mechanisms include blue light's effect on melatonin and alertness, the brain's adaptation to light variation, and the way materials reflect, absorb, or transmit light to reveal texture, form, and color.

findings.antecedent: Articulation and interplay of light and shadow
findings.consequent: Potential experiences in contemporary architecture
findings.mechanism: Homogeneous and standard lighting solutions deny users sensorial and perceptual stimulation developed through lighting variability and contrast.
findings.quote: Homogeneous and standard lighting solutions deny users sensorial and perceptual stimulation developed through lighting variability and contrast.

findings.antecedent: Expression of sunlight, artificial light, architectural form, physical properties of material, and spatial ambiance
findings.consequent: Architectural experience and spatial perception
findings.mechanism: These elements, when creatively integrated, create perceptually fluid environments that transform user experience throughout the day.
findings.quote: The expression of sunlight, artificial light, architectural form, the physical properties of material, and spatial ambiance improves the architectural experience and spatial perception throughout the day.

findings.antecedent: Deep shadows and darkness
findings.consequent: Sharpness of vision, depth and distance perception, unconscious peripheral vision and tactile fantasy
findings.mechanism: Darkness dims vision, thereby heightening other senses and inviting a more imaginative and tactile engagement with space.
findings.quote: “Deep shadows and darkness are essential, because they dim the sharpness of vision, make depth and distance, and invite unconscious peripheral vision and tactile fantasy”

findings.antecedent: Dissimilar lighting scenarios in architectural environments
findings.consequent: Sensorial stimulation, engagement of user’s eye, mind and body
findings.mechanism: Varied lighting conditions provide different forms of stimulation, preventing habituation and enriching the overall experience.
findings.quote: Designing architectural environments that consist of dissimilar lighting scenarios provides different forms of sensorial stimulation that engage the user’s eye, mind and body.

findings.antecedent: Different colours of light (electromagnetic spectrum)
findings.consequent: Way users perceive and experience the world, bodily functions (e.g., melatonin secretion)
findings.mechanism: Each band of colored light has distinct characteristics that affect human perception and physiology (e.g., blue light secretes melatonin for alertness).
findings.quote: Research has shown that different colours light of the electromagnetic spectrum influence the way users perceive and experience the world them. Blue light has been shown to secrete the production of melatonin, and thus enables the body to feel more alert and awake.

findings.antecedent: Daylight integration in spaces
findings.consequent: People’s visual and biological experiences, overall performance, productivity and comfort of users, regulation of circadian rhythms
findings.mechanism: Daylight provides mental and visual stimulation necessary for proper circadian rhythm regulation, impacting hormones like serotonin and melatonin.
findings.quote: Design integration of daylight can drastically improve people’s visual and biological experiences (Boubekri 2014).

findings.antecedent: Homogeneous bright light
findings.consequent: Imagination, experience of being, sense of place
findings.mechanism: Uniform light paralyzes imagination and weakens the experience of being, similar to how homogenized space diminishes the sense of place.
findings.quote: “Homogeneous bright light paralyses the imagination in the same way that homogenization of space weakens the experience of being, and wipes away the sense of place”

findings.antecedent: Lower light intensity and uneven distribution in public spaces
findings.consequent: Enjoyment of public spaces
findings.mechanism: Variability and contrast in lighting create more engaging and stimulating environments, which are preferred over uniformly bright spaces.
findings.quote: “Most contemporary public spaces would become more enjoyable through a lower light intensity and its uneven distribution”

findings.antecedent: Material properties (opaque, transparent, translucent, reflective)
findings.consequent: Characteristics of light (absorbed, reflected, refracted, transmitted), spatial experience
findings.mechanism: The physical properties of materials dictate how light interacts with them, revealing unique characteristics (color, texture, form) and transforming perception throughout the day.
findings.quote: is absorbed, reflected, refracted, and transmitted through a material describe the characteristics of a material and can be categorized as being opaque, transparent, translucent or reflective material.

findings.antecedent: Creative lighting design expression
findings.consequent: Perceptual stimulation, enriched architectural environment and user experience
findings.mechanism: By varying lighting conditions and integrating light with architectural elements, environments perceptually transform throughout the day, engaging the eye, mind, and body.
findings.quote: Creative lighting design expression provides perceptual stimulation that enriches the architectural environment and user experience as environments perceptually transform throughout the day.

findings.antecedent: Integration of light and shadow as a design medium
findings.consequent: Architectural environments, spatial experiences
findings.mechanism: Light and shadow, when intentionally designed, can define spatial boundaries, create focal points, and evoke specific emotional and perceptual responses, making environments perceptually fluid.
findings.quote: This thesis advocates the importance of expressing light and shadow as a design medium to shape architectural environments.

findings.antecedent: Lighting variation and diversity within architecture
findings.consequent: Enrichment of architectural environment, introduction of layers of experiential moment
findings.mechanism: The human eye constantly adapts to various lighting stimuli; variation provides unique sensorial experiences as conditions change throughout the day.
findings.quote: Lighting variation and diversity within architecture create opportunity to enrich the architectural environment and introduce layers of experiential moment as the lighting condition changes throughout the day.

findings.antecedent: Non-homogeneous environments
findings.consequent: Overall architectural experience, physiological and psychological well-being of the user
findings.mechanism: The eye's adjustable sensors respond to different visual lighting stimulation, and the brain distinguishes subtle changes, leading to a richer and more complex understanding of space.
findings.quote: In the book Environmental Diversity in Architecture, Mary Ann Steane and Koen Steemers describe the importance of designing non-homogeneous environments in order to improve the overall architectural experience, as well as its physiological and psychological well-being of the user.

findings.antecedent: Exposure to unstructured uniform stimulation fields (Ganzfeld effect)
findings.consequent: Brain amplifying neural noise, missing visual signals
findings.mechanism: The brain attempts to compensate for a lack of visual input by generating its own signals, leading to distorted perception.
findings.quote: Known as the Ganzfeld effect, the exposure to unstructured uniform stimulation fields results in the brain amplifying neural noise in order to provide missing visual signals.

findings.antecedent: Diverse luminance in the field of view
findings.consequent: Perception of space as 'pleasant', 'cheerful', 'bright', 'radiant', 'clear', 'visually warm' and 'strong'
findings.mechanism: Variability in light provides visual stimulation that engages the eye, mind, and body, leading to more positive spatial perceptions.
findings.quote: “The more diverse the luminance in the field of view, the more ‘pleasant’, ‘cheerful’, ‘bright’, ‘radiant’, ‘clear’, ‘visually warm’ and ‘strong’ the space to appears”

findings.antecedent: Perceptual qualities (contrast and temporal variability) of light
findings.consequent: Appreciation of architectural space
findings.mechanism: These qualities add depth to complex geometries and infuse otherwise static interior spaces with shifting compositions of light and shadow, making the space more engaging.
findings.quote: “Perceptual qualities such as contrast and temporal variability are essential to our appreciation of architectural space; natural illumination adds depths to complex geometries and infuses otherwise static interior spaces with shifting compositions of light and shadow”

findings.antecedent: Dynamic lighting conditions throughout the day
findings.consequent: Architectural space as a dynamic design element, new experiential opportunities
findings.mechanism: The ever-changing nature of light provides architects with a fluid medium to create transforming environments that offer varied experiences.
findings.quote: The ever-changing lighting conditions throughout the day offers architects a dynamic design element, providing new experiential opportunities through the expression of both sunlight and artificial light.

findings.antecedent: Interplay of light and shadow
findings.consequent: Experiential depth in built form
findings.mechanism: Dark shadows overlapping with light lines create a dynamic interaction that enriches the perception of space beyond mere form.
findings.quote: The interplay of light and shadow provides the built form with experiential depth as dark shadows overlap with light lines, and as the whole interaction is dynamic throughout the day.

findings.antecedent: Darkness (reducing visual sharpness)
findings.consequent: Enrichment of architectural experience, necessity of other senses to perceive spatial environments
findings.mechanism: By diminishing visual clarity, darkness forces reliance on other sensory modalities, leading to a more profound and multi-sensory engagement with space.
findings.quote: the use of darkness enriches the architectural experience by reducing the sharpness of our vision, necessitating the use of our other senses to perceive spatial environments.

findings.antecedent: Artificial illumination
findings.consequent: Built environment appearing as illuminated objects on the street, new spatial experiences and design expressions
findings.mechanism: At night, artificial light allows buildings to become luminous objects, revealing their interiors and creating new perceptual experiences distinct from daylight.
findings.quote: night enables the built environment to appear as illuminated objects on the street. James Carpenter, a light artist and designer believes that glass is one of the most intriguing material to work with, “The aim is to extend the experience of the boundary between the interior and exterior well beyond the physical depth of the building skin by understanding the optical and perceptual transition that occurs at that boundary”

findings.antecedent: Glass facades
findings.consequent: Depth of perception between interior and exterior environments
findings.mechanism: Glass allows for multiple layers of objects, surfaces, and light fixtures to be composed into a single framed view, blurring boundaries and influencing user perception.
findings.quote: Glass can blur the boundary between interior and exterior environments, extending the perception of space between the two environments.

findings.antecedent: Louvre system (slightly angled)
findings.consequent: Light penetration into collaborative space, direct light exposure in office workstation, continuous facade composition, spatial lighting conditions
findings.mechanism: The rotation and angling of louvres allow for controlled light mediation, enabling more light into collaborative areas while reducing direct exposure in workstations, creating varied interior lighting conditions.
findings.quote: The louvre is designed to allow for more light to penetrate the collaborative space, whereas the louvres slightly rotate along the office work station to reduce direct light exposure within the space. This variation within the façade design produce different spatial lighting condition seen within the interior through the use of daylight as well as the exterior.

findings.antecedent: Office hub design (light, material, form)
findings.consequent: Unique characteristics and design of individual rooms, distinct spatial ambiance and lighting condition, spatial identity, programmatic activity support
findings.mechanism: By curating light, material, and form within each space, a specific lighting ambiance is created that supports the intended function and provides a unique identity to the room.
findings.quote: The design of the office hub utilizes light, material and form to reveal the unique characteristics and design of the individual rooms. Within each space, a unique spatial ambiance and lighting condition are expressed to support the programmatic activity as well as create a spatial identity within the building.

findings.antecedent: Low light ambiance (e.g., private meeting room)
findings.consequent: Sensorial environment, desensitization of eye, mind, and body, focus on illuminated work/digital media, revelation of textural characteristics
findings.mechanism: Reducing visual stimulation in a 'cave-like' setting shifts focus to other senses and specific illuminated elements, enhancing intimacy and concentration.
findings.quote: A cave like spatial experience is perceived through the dark lighting condition and illumination from above. A sensorial environment is experienced within the meeting room as the low light ambiance desensitize the eye, mind, and body.

findings.antecedent: High illumination (e.g., workstation with channel glass)
findings.consequent: Refreshing and energized environment, alertness
findings.mechanism: Diffuse sunlight and a soft glow at night maintain high light levels throughout the day, promoting alertness and a sense of vitality.
findings.quote: The workstation is designed to receive a high amount illumination throughout the day, making the environment appear refreshing and energized with light.

findings.antecedent: Seasonal changes in solar angles (e.g., Toronto winter)
findings.consequent: Amount of light buildings receive, incidence of Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD), user mood and physical aptitude
findings.mechanism: Lesser light exposure during winter can negatively impact human physiology and psychology, leading to SAD, which the built environment can counter through light integration.
findings.quote: During the winter, lesser light exposure can cause seasonal affective disorder (SAD), which has a negative impact on humans’ overall mood and physical aptitude.

testable_hypotheses_or_predictions: Measuring physiological responses (e.g., cortisol, heart rate variability) and self-reported mood in environments with varying light and shadow conditions versus homogeneous lighting.
Assessing cognitive performance (e.g., attention, creativity, problem-solving) in office spaces designed with dynamic light/shadow interplay compared to standard uniform lighting.
Evaluating user preference and perceived restorativeness for architectural spaces that integrate light and shadow as a design medium, across different times of day.

Quantifying the impact of specific material properties (e.g., translucency, reflectivity, texture) on perceived spatial ambiance and user experience under different natural and artificial lighting conditions.
Investigating the effect of blue light integration in working environments on alertness and productivity during specific times of day, and its impact on sleep quality.
Comparing the incidence of Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD) symptoms and overall well-being in buildings with varying degrees of daylight integration during winter months.
Analyzing the effectiveness of louvre systems and other light filtration devices in modulating light and shadow patterns to create desired spatial experiences and reduce glare.
bridge_warrants: The paper connects light and shadow expression to human perception and experience, aligning with predictive processing theories where environmental variability influences prediction error and engagement.
It links dynamic lighting conditions to chronobiological regulation, specifically circadian rhythms and melatonin production, impacting alertness and well-being.
The discussion of sensorial stimulation and the engagement of the body and mind bridges to interoceptive and embodied cognition frameworks.
The critique of homogeneous lighting and advocacy for varied environments relates to attention restoration theory and the need for cognitive stimulation.
The emphasis on material properties and their interaction with light connects to multisensory integration, where visual and haptic cues combine to form material perception.
methodological_critiques: The evaluation of architectural lighting in contemporary architecture increasingly follows quantifiable design reasoning, neglecting the importance of qualitative lighting design in shaping architectural environment and experience.
Homogeneous and standard lighting solutions, often driven by codes and standards, deprive users of sensorial and perceptual stimulation developed through lighting variability and contrast.

The pervasive use of glass curtain walls and artificial illumination has saturated contemporary architecture with light, reducing the presence of shadow and depriving users of potential experiences through light/shadow interplay.
Modern architecture's preoccupation with formal design has neglected material expression, reducing the interplay of light and shadow through impurities and imperfections.
model_structure: The thesis proposes a conceptual framework where architectural design elements (form, material, apertures) are vehicles for light and shadow expression. This expression, modulated by natural (solar orientation, day/night cycle) and artificial light, creates diverse spatial lighting conditions. These conditions, in turn, influence user perception, experience, and well-being by providing sensorial and perceptual stimulation, engaging the eye, mind, and body, and supporting chronobiological regulation. The framework implicitly suggests a feedback loop where enhanced user experience informs future design choices.
limitations: The current architectural practice's focus on quantifiable metrics for lighting design limits the exploration and integration of qualitative lighting expressions.
The widespread use of modern glazing and artificial illumination has led to light saturation, depriving users of the experiential potential of light and shadow interplay.
Traditional office typologies, focused on function and efficiency with uniform light distribution, fail to support the evolving collaborative and mobile working cultures of the 21st century.

mechanism_chain.description: The paper conceptually outlines how the articulation and interplay of light and shadow, specifically through their contrast, luminosity, and porosity, mediate the potential experiences within contemporary architectural spaces.
